name: Call Spread Overwrite
summary: Long stock with a short call against it plus a further-OTM long call, so the position is capped between the two strikes but participates again in a large rally - a covered call that gives the right tail back.

legs.strike_rule: call delta 0.08-0.12, at least 5% above the short call (the upside re-entry)

max_profit: UNLIMITED above the long call strike; between the strikes it is capped at (short strike - basis + net credit) x 100
max_loss: (basis - net credit) x 100 if the shares go to zero - the same downside as owning the stock, less the credit

greeks.delta: +60 to +75 per unit, rising back toward +100 above the long call
greeks.gamma: negative between the strikes, positive above the long strike
greeks.theta: positive while spot is below the short strike

when_to_use: When a covered call is wanted for income but the name has a real melt-up or takeover tail you refuse to give away - high-beta single names, or ETFs in a strong uptrend where a plain overwrite has been repeatedly run over.
entry_rules: Shares already held, 100 per unit, unencumbered (not pledged to another structure).
Short call delta 0.25-0.35; long call delta 0.08-0.12; distance between strikes >= 5% of spot.
Net credit > 0 after paying for the long call - if the long call costs more than the short brings in, use a plain covered call instead.
Short strike >= basis x 1.02 so assignment cannot lock in a loss on the shares.
Both option legs same expiry, OI >= 250 each, submitted as one 2-leg MLeg order against the existing shares.
No entry with an ex-dividend date inside 5 trading days of expiration.
management_rules: Buy back the short call at 50-70% of its premium and re-write on the next cycle.
If spot exceeds the short strike by more than 1 x ATR(14), roll the short call up and out for a credit once; leave the long call alone.
Sell the long call and revert to a plain covered call if its delta falls below 0.03 with more than 21 DTE left - it has stopped being worth the capital.
Close both option legs together when the shares are sold.
exit_rules: ASSIGNMENT GUARD: buy the short call back by 15:30 ET on expiration day whenever it is ITM - assignment would sell the shares and leave a naked long call plus an unwanted flat position.
Close the short call immediately when its extrinsic value < $0.10 or delta >= 0.85.
Ex-dividend guard: close the short call the session before any ex-dividend date while it is ITM.
Close the long call rather than letting it auto-exercise; exercise would buy 100 more shares.
assignment_risk: One short call, fully covered by shares. Early assignment sells the shares at the short strike, which is not a loss but is an unplanned liquidation that also strands the long call. The extrinsic and ex-dividend guards exist to prevent it.
buying_power: Shares plus the long call's debit; the short call is share-covered, so no additional requirement. Level 3 (level 2 would cover the short call; the long call adds nothing).
liquidity_needs: A chain that still quotes tightly at 0.10 delta - ETFs and liquid mega-caps; the long call is the leg most likely to be a wide market.
common_mistakes: Buying the upper call so far out that it is lottery-ticket junk and never pays; paying a net debit and calling it income; forgetting the long call exists when the shares are sold.
zero_dte_notes: Pointless at 0DTE - the whole value of the structure is the multi-week upside tail.
family: Completeness gap-fill (cross-family): ratio/naked-financed put and call structures, quantity-unbalanced condors and strangles, stock+option overlays and monetizations, capital-protection and hybrid builds, 0DTE four-leg income, volatility-surface and relative-value trades, event-driven overlays, and roll/adjustment structures
